name: Trequartista 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes to the wide midfielders or forwards, simply and quickly.
Support full-back provides width and cover behind the wide midfielder.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Wide midfielder (Support) works hard on the flank and covers for the trequartista's lack of defensive work.
Defensive central midfielder screens the defence.
Box-to-box midfielder supports both forwards with runs from deep.
Wide midfielder (Support) on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Trequartista drops off the front and roams to create chances; he does not press or track back.
Pressing forward (Support) presses the defenders and links with the trequartista.

description: A 4-4-2 in which one striker is a trequartista who drops off and creates, paired with a pressing forward who does the running.
whyGood: The trequartista supplies the creativity a two-striker team often lacks, and his partner and the hard-working wide midfielders cover his defensive gaps.
whyThisShape: The trequartista plays as a striker but drops off and roams behind his partner, so the team plays like a 4-4-1-1 in attack and a 4-4-2 out of possession, except that he does not defend. The pressing forward presses for both, and the hard-working wide midfielders and midfield pair keep the team compact behind them.
whenToUse: When you have a creative forward who is not a natural goalscorer, and a partner with pace and work rate.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that overload the midfield, since the trequartista does not track back; and when your wide midfielders lack the stamina to cover.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Full Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: A genuinely high-quality Trequartista with strong vision, technique, first touch, decisions and passing
A Pressing Forward partner with exceptional work rate and enough stamina, aggression and teamwork to press for both forwards
Wide midfielders with the stamina and work rate to compensate for the Trequartista's defensive freedom
A disciplined Central Midfielder (Defend) behind an energetic Box-to-Box runner
Enough technical quality in the front pair to make Work Ball Into Box worthwhile
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
